hypothesis: A pre-registered hypothesis under test, not an edge claim. PATH 1 (own capital at IBKR, multi-day holds allowed): an inverse-volatility (risk-parity) portfolio of 7 asset classes with a 10-month trend filter (an asset below its 10-month average is replaced by short-term Treasuries) and a 10% portfolio volatility target delivers a net excess-of-cash return with a higher Sharpe than 60/40 at the same volatility. Known published family (Faber 2007 tactical asset allocation; Asness-Frazzini-Pedersen 2012 risk parity; Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012). Nearest inherited relative: the ETF trend study (references/trend-following-etf.md, OOS 2016-11..2026-09, long/short Sharpe 0.61), which this row extends with risk parity, bonds/gold/commodities and a different filter.
rules: Data: daily total-return levels USLCAP, LTT, ITT, GLSTOCK, GLBOND, GOLDPM, CMDTY (risky) and STT (cash) from daily_assets_1970_2026, used only from 1992-01-02 (observed series begin 1991-10-29). Daily return r = level_t/level_(t-1) - 1. At the close of the last trading day of each month m: (1) for each risky asset, sigma_i = standard deviation of its last 63 daily returns x sqrt(252); raw weight w_i = (1/sigma_i) / sum_j(1/sigma_j); (2) trend filter: if level_t < mean of its last 210 daily levels, that asset's weight moves to STT; (3) portfolio scale k = 0.10 / sigma_p where sigma_p = sqrt(252) x standard deviation of the last 63 daily returns of the month-end weight vector applied to past returns; k capped at 1.5, floored at 0.25; final weights k x w (risky and STT slots); borrowing above 1.0 total exposure pays STT return + 1.0% a year. Weights apply from the next trading day's return through the next month end (no look-ahead: everything uses data through the decision close). Portfolio daily return = sum(weights x returns) - financing - costs; costs = 2 bp per side on the absolute change in each weight at each rebalance (IBKR ETF commission+spread floor); 2x run doubles costs. Headline series: daily portfolio return minus STT daily return (excess of cash).
parameters: risky set of 7; vol lookback 63d; trend lookback 210d; target vol 10%; k in [0.25, 1.5]; monthly rebalance; borrow spread 1%/yr; cost 2 bp per side
grid: single configuration (no in-sample selection; IS used for nothing but the IS report)
instruments: USLCAP, LTT, ITT, GLSTOCK, GLBOND, GOLDPM, CMDTY (ETF proxies at IBKR: SPY/IVV, TLT, IEF, ACWX/VEU, BNDX, GLD, DBC); cash STT
vol_scaler: ex-ante 63-day realized portfolio vol at each month end, target 10%, cap 1.5x, floor 0.25x
cost_model: 2 bp per side on traded notional at each monthly rebalance + borrow cost STT+1%/yr above 100% exposure; 2x run attached
decision_rule: Gate v2 criterion 4 on the OOS daily excess-of-cash series: PASS Gate 3 iff t_min(iid, NW lag 21) >= 3.6807 AND stationary-bootstrap lower bound at 0.05/430 (>= 430,000 draws, mean block 20) > 0 AND 2x-cost t >= 1.65; else FAIL. Reported at the WEAKER OWN-CAPITAL STANDARD regardless (pre-specified, no count): net excess Sharpe with Mertens/Opdyke 90% CI, CAGR and max drawdown, and the same statistics for 60/40 USLCAP/ITT (monthly rebalance, costs 2 bp per side) scaled ex post to the strategy's OOS realized volatility; alpha t of the strategy's daily excess return regressed on 60/40's daily excess return (NW lag 21); sub-periods 2010-01..2016-10 (not displayed by the inherited ETF study) and 2016-11..2024-12 (derivative window) reported separately.
notes: Evidence window: the inherited ETF study displays 2016-11..2026-09 on ETFs; this row's OOS 2016-11..2024-12 overlaps it and is DERIVATIVE; the 2010-01..2016-10 sub-period is the clean window. Realistic expectation: excess Sharpe 0.5-0.9, so criterion 4 power is low (t ~ 0.7 x sqrt(15) ~ 2.7 < 3.68): a FAIL here is expected even if the portfolio is useful for own capital; the own-capital standard (Sharpe and drawdown vs 60/40 at equal vol) is what Itamar asked for. Hold-out 2025-01..2026-09 is not read.
